title: Low-touch slab pricing: HC impact prototype (Jul 2026)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working prototype (sheet-style) to model a low-touch slab pricing product (think: simple tiered slabs for small/SMB customers) and estimate the marginal headcount and operating impact for the Platform & Sales motions. Goal: fast experiment to check whether slab pricing (with minimal onboarding/customer success) can scale economically without large Dedicated conversion funnels.

Notes / context (quick):
- Why this is new: current models focus on per-token/meters for higher-touch customers. We need a simpler bucketed slab for self-serve customers to increase adoption while reducing support overhead.
- Risk: slab pricing can encourage surprising token consumption; mitigation by conservative slab sizing + throttles.
- Audience: FP&A, RevOps, Pricing PM, small-business GTM lead.

Assumptions (editable cells in the sheet):
- Time horizon: 12 months (Jul2026 - Jun2027).
- Slab definitions (example):
  * SLAB A (Starter): up to 100k tokens/mo — price = $49/mo
  * SLAB B (Growth): 100k-1M tokens/mo — price = $249/mo
  * SLAB C (Scale): 1M-5M tokens/mo — price = $749/mo
- Average tokens per customer (est): Starter 60k, Growth 500k, Scale 2.2M
- Churn: Starter 6%/mo, Growth 4%/mo, Scale 3%/mo
- Conversion from trial -> paying: Starter 8%, Growth 4%, Scale 1%
- CAC (blended, paid growth channels): Starter $35, Growth $120, Scale $450
- Incremental support/service load: Starter 0.1 FTE per 1k customers, Growth 0.5 FTE per 1k customers, Scale 1.0 FTE per 100 customers (onboarding needs)
- Average fully-burdened engineer cost: $200k/year -> $16.7k/month
- Customer success / onboarding fully-burdened cost: $150k/year -> $12.5k/month
- Infra unit costs: estimate token cost $0.000012 per token (hosted infra blended) — this is conservative.

Primary sheet tabs (planned):
- Inputs: parameters above (editable) and experiment toggles (throttles, usage caps).
- Cohort sims: month-by-month customer counts, MRR, churn, ARR build.
- HC impact: hires needed by month (SWE infra, CS, support) to maintain SLA targets per slab.
- Sensitivity: 3x3 grid varying price +/- 25% and token cost +/- 50%.
- KPI summary: GM%, CAC payback months, contribution margin per slab.

Quick scenario snapshots (one-year aggregated):
- Base: 10k Starter customers, 1.2k Growth, 120 Scale (end of year) -> MRR = Starter(10k*$49)= $490k + Growth(1.2k*$249)= $298.8k + Scale(120*$749)= $89.9k => total MRR ~ $878.7k -> ARR ~ $10.5M.
- Low-adoption: Starter 4k, Growth 400, Scale 30 -> ARR ~ $3.6M.
- High-adoption: Starter 25k, Growth 3k, Scale 400 -> ARR ~ $23.1M.

Headcount impact (summary):
- Base scenario hires (net new over 12 months):
  * Growth engineering (platform/runtime) to support slab throttles and metering: 2 SWE (mid/senior) -> estimated run rate cost: $400k/yr.
  * Customer success (low-touch scale means small but non-zero onboarding): 3 CSMs -> $375k/yr.
  * Support (tier 1 + ops): 4 engineers -> $600k/yr.
  * Pricing/analytics (part-time): 0.5 FTE -> $75k/yr.
  Total incremental HC cost (annualized) ~ $1.45M (rough) -> ~13.8% of ARR in base scenario.

Sensitivity snippets (calculation notes):
- Margin per slab = price - (token_cost * expected_tokens_per_customer) - per-customer Opex allocation (support/CS/infra).
- For Starter: token cost per month = 60k * $0.000012 = $0.72/mo (negligible), but per-customer fixed overhead (tiny overhead + billing) assumed $8/mo -> gross margin per Starter ~ $49 - $8.72 = $40.28 -> GM% ~ 82%.
- For Growth: token cost = 500k * $0.000012 = $6/mo -> plus overhead $25/mo -> GM ~ $249 - $31 = $218 -> GM% ~ 88%.
- For Scale: token cost = 2.2M * $0.000012 = $26.4/mo -> overhead $150/mo (onboarding/solutions) -> GM ~ $749 - $176.4 = $572.6 -> GM% ~ 76%.

Key trade-offs and open questions (notes to self):
- Do we allow burst overages? If yes, how priced (per-token or automated throttle)? Overages create noise in predictability.
- How to route heavy customers: automated suggest to upgrade to Dedicated / Dedicated conversion play (ops + sales).
- Support SLAs: low-touch implies <48h async and no guaranteed latency SLA. But will that leak to product reputation?
- Should we offer an annual prepay discount? What lift does it provide on CAC payback? Quick model: 10% prepay reduces churn for Starter by ~1.5ppt.

Experiment plan (next 60 days):
1) Build configurable sheet (this doc) and link to Confluence page for assumptions. Owner: Maya.
2) Run sensitivity grid across price +/- 25%, token_cost +/-50% and churn +/-2ppt. Deliverable: heatmap of contribution margin and threshold where HC must increase by +1 FTE. Owner: Finance analyst (Priya). Due: Jul 30.
3) Small A/B test in US region: expose slab pricing as optional checkout for 5k trial users. Track conversion to paying and support ticket rate. Owner: Growth (Ethan). Start: Aug 10.
4) If positive (CAC payback < 6mo and GM% > 65%), prepare a Dedicated conversion playbook for Growth slab customers. Owner: Solutions Eng. Due: Sep 15.

Appendix: quick calculation snippets (for copy into Excel):
- CAC payback (months) = CAC / (ARPU_monthly * contribution_margin%).
- Example Starter: CAC $35 / ($49 * 0.82) = 0.87 months -> super fast but must be validated vs actual retention.

TODOs / outstanding data pulls:
- Actual token cost by model family (embedding vs generation) from infra billing (request: FIN-ops export).
- Real support ticket rates per 1k customers from support BI for prior launch (ask SRE for triage times).
- Channel mix CAC by cohort (organic vs paid).
- Legal review on “throttle” terms in TOS (optional).

Comments (ongoing):
- Diego: flagged that Starter churn assumption might be optimistic; suggested stress test at 10%/mo.
- Ethan: wants a simple billing UX prototype before A/B starts; stub checkout in the growth funnel.

Bottom line (early):
- Slab pricing looks promising for low-touch adoption: very favorable unit economics for Starter & Growth on paper due to low token costs. The main lever is controlling onboarding/support cost (keep low-touch).
- Critical sensitivity: if token cost rises (more expensive models used by customers) or if churn is higher than expected, GC margins compress quickly and HC needs increase to handle support/ops.

Version history / quick notes:
- 2026-07-08: initial prototype (Maya)
